submission_readiness.summary: The synthetic Part 135 submission contains core fleet, pilot, loss, operations, safety, and maintenance information, but valuation support, one recurrent-training record, and a detailed Caribbean-operations breakdown are missing.

exposure_summary.summary: The synthetic fleet comprises 28 aircraft with USD 436 million of stated hull value, a USD 55 million largest single-aircraft value, and projected utilization of 11,500 hours.

hull_asset_analysis.summary: Hull concentration and valuation changes warrant authorized review before program structure or capacity decisions.
issues: N650PJ is represented at USD 55 million versus USD 47.5 million in the prior year, but supporting valuation evidence is not included.
Two Gulfstream G650ER aircraft represent USD 110 million of the USD 436 million total stated hull value.
Repair-cost, parts-availability, downtime, and replacement-cost assumptions are not independently validated by this demonstration.

missing_information: Updated supporting valuation documentation for N650PJ and any other materially revalued aircraft.
Detailed Caribbean operations breakdown, including airports, frequency, seasonality, and overnight exposure.

risk_flags.fact: The synthetic submission reports USD 436 million in total hull value, including two Gulfstream G650ER aircraft with USD 110 million of combined stated value.
risk_flags.why_review: An authorized reviewer should assess single-aircraft and fleet concentration relative to appetite, capacity, repair severity, and program structure.

risk_flags.fact: Projected policy-year flight hours are 11,500 versus 8,900 in the prior year, a 29.2% increase.
risk_flags.why_review: The operational change should be validated and assessed for its effect on frequency exposure, pricing assumptions, and authority.

risk_flags.fact: Caribbean operations represent 14% of synthetic flight activity.
risk_flags.why_review: Airport mix, weather, catastrophe, security, and jurisdictional factors require qualified review.

risk_flags.fact: Training records are represented as complete for 46 of 47 named pilots; Pilot 27 recurrent-training documentation is missing.
risk_flags.why_review: Pilot qualification and recurrent-training evidence should be completed before any consequential underwriting action.

risk_flags.fact: The synthetic five-year loss history includes a USD 4.8 million runway-excursion hull loss in 2025.
risk_flags.why_review: A qualified reviewer should assess cause, corrective action, recurrence potential, and relevance to current operations.

delegated_authority_review.summary: The submission exceeds multiple illustrative delegated-authority thresholds and should be routed to an authorized carrier or senior underwriting reviewer.
reasons: USD 55 million largest single-aircraft hull exceeds the synthetic USD 50 million threshold.
USD 500 million requested liability limit exceeds the synthetic USD 300 million threshold.
14% Caribbean flight share exceeds the synthetic 10% threshold.
29.2% projected utilization increase exceeds the synthetic 25% threshold.
delegated_authority_review.disclaimer: Illustrative referral logic only; this is not actual carrier authority or appetite.

fac_review.summary: Potential facultative or additional-capacity review is indicated by the synthetic fleet concentration and requested liability limit, but no placement or capacity decision can be made from this demonstration.
issues: Primary/program structure and target facultative layer are not finalized.
Capacity need should be assessed by an authorized underwriting or reinsurance professional after missing information is resolved.
Any FAC terms must be reconciled with the underlying policy wording and actual carrier/reinsurer authority.

recommended_next_action: Obtain the missing valuation, training, and Caribbean-operations information, validate the material utilization change, and route the file to an authorized senior underwriting/capacity reviewer for appetite, authority, program-structure, and any facultative assessment.
limitations: No pricing, binding, declining, capacity, coverage, legal, sanctions, regulatory, actuarial, claims, or engineering determination is made.
Hull values, repair-cost assumptions, pilot qualifications, operational representations, and delegated-authority thresholds require independent validation.
